_The Walking Dead_ was renewed by AMC for a 16-episode eighth season on October 16, 2016.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-ew_s8-4) Production began on April 25, 2017, in Atlanta, Georgia.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-5) On July 12, 2017, production was shut down after stuntman John Bernecker was killed, after falling more than 20 feet onto a concrete floor.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-6) Production resumed on July 17.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-7) The season premiere, which also serves as the series' milestone 100th episode, was directed by executive producer Greg Nicotero.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-Director801-8)

In November 2017, it was announced that Lennie James who portrays Morgan Jones, would be leaving _The Walking Dead_ after the conclusion of this season, and would join the cast of the spin-off series _Fear the Walking Dead_ for its fourth season.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-9) The eighth season also features the departures of series regulars Chandler Riggs (Carl Grimes), Steven Ogg (Simon), and Austin Amelio (Dwight). Riggs' final episode is the mid-season premiere where his character is killed off, which is a deviation from the comic book, where his character is still alive. His death received negative reactions from critics and fans.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-10) Ogg's final episode is the penultimate episode of the season, where his character is killed by Negan.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-11) Amelio departed the series after the season finale, and in January 2019, it was confirmed he would join the cast of _Fear the Walking Dead_.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-12)
The first trailer for the season was released on July 21, 2017 at San Diego Comic-Con. The second trailer was released on February 1, 2018 for the second part of the season.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-29)
On March 15, 2018, it was announced that the season finale and the fourth season premiere of _Fear the Walking Dead_ would be screened at AMC, Regal, and Cinemark theaters across the United States on April 15, the same day as the TV airing, for "Survival Sunday: _The Walking Dead_&_Fear the Walking Dead_". The episodes marked the first crossover between the two series. The cinema screening also included an extra half-hour of exclusive bonus content.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-Cinema-30)

_The Walking Dead_ was renewed by AMC for a 16-episode eighth season on October 16, 2016.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-ew_s8-4) Production began on April 25, 2017, in Atlanta, Georgia.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-5) On July 12, 2017, production was shut down after stuntman John Bernecker was killed, after falling more than 20 feet onto a concrete floor.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-6) Production resumed on July 17.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-7) The season premiere, which also serves as the series' milestone 100th episode, was directed by executive producer Greg Nicotero.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-Director801-8)
texts.8:
#### Alexandria Safe-Zone
In November 2017, it was announced that Lennie James who portrays Morgan Jones, would be leaving _The Walking Dead_ after the conclusion of this season, and would join the cast of the spin-off series _Fear the Walking Dead_ for its fourth season.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-9) The eighth season also features the departures of series regulars Chandler Riggs (Carl Grimes), Steven Ogg (Simon), and Austin Amelio (Dwight). Riggs' final episode is the mid-season premiere where his character is killed off, which is a deviation from the comic book, where his character is still alive. His death received negative reactions from critics and fans.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-10) Ogg's final episode is the penultimate episode of the season, where his character is killed by Negan.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-11) Amelio departed the series after the season finale, and in January 2019, it was confirmed he would join the cast of _Fear the Walking Dead_.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-12)
The first trailer for the season was released on July 21, 2017 at San Diego Comic-Con. The second trailer was released on February 1, 2018 for the second part of the season.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-29)
On March 15, 2018, it was announced that the season finale and the fourth season premiere of _Fear the Walking Dead_ would be screened at AMC, Regal, and Cinemark theaters across the United States on April 15, the same day as the TV airing, for "Survival Sunday: _The Walking Dead_&_Fear the Walking Dead_". The episodes marked the first crossover between the two series. The cinema screening also included an extra half-hour of exclusive bonus content.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-Cinema-30)

The eighth season of _The Walking Dead_ received mixed reviews from critics. On Rotten Tomatoes, the season holds a score of 65% with an average rating of 6.65 out of 10 based on 447 reviews. The site's critical consensus reads: "_The Walking Dead_'s eighth season energizes its characters with some much-needed angst and action, though it's still occasionally choppy and lacking forward-moving plot progression."[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-RT_S8-31)

For the 44th Saturn Awards, the eighth season of _The Walking Dead_ received seven nominations, winning two. It won Best Horror Television Series and Best Performance by a Younger Actor in a Television Series (Chandler Riggs).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-S44-1) The nominations were for Best Actor on Television (Andrew Lincoln), Best Supporting Actor on Television (Khary Payton), Best Supporting Actress on Television (Danai Gurira and Melissa McBride), and Best Guest Starring Role on Television (Jeffrey Dean Morgan).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-32)
The first half of the season was nominated for Outstanding Performance by a Stunt Ensemble in a Television Series at the 24th Screen Actors Guild Awards.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-33)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia  
Map of the United States with Georgia highlighted
Georgia is a state located in the Southern United States. According to the 2020 United States census, Georgia was the 8th most populous state with 10,711,908 inhabitants and the 21st largest by land area spanning 57,513.49 square miles (148,959.3 km2) of land.[1] Georgia is divided into 159 counties and contains 535 municipalities consisting of cities, towns, consolidated city-counties, and consolidated cities.[2] [3]
There is no legal difference in Georgia between cities and towns.[4] Eight municipalities have merged with their counties to form consolidated city-counties: Athens with Clarke County, Augusta with Richmond County, Columbus with Muscogee County, Cusseta with Chattahoochee County, Georgetown with Quitman County, Macon with Bibb County, Statenville with Echols County, and Webster County unified government with Webster County. Athens and Augusta also have municipalities independent of the consolidated governments and are considered consolidated cities.[2]
The largest municipality by population in Georgia is Atlanta, with 498,715 residents, and the smallest municipality by population is Aldora, with 0 residents, although the actual estimated population is at 103, due to a "0% self-response rate".[3] The largest municipality by land area is Augusta, a consolidated city-county, which spans 302.47 mi2 (783.4 km2), and Edge Hill and Santa Claus are tied for the smallest, at 0.18 mi2 (0.47 km2) each.[1][a]

## About Georgia
In Georgia, counties are governed by elected boards of commissioners or sole commissioners, responsible for countywide issues such as public health, emergency services, infrastructure, and county law enforcement. For example, Fulton County, encompassing Atlanta, is managed by a board of commissioners with a county manager who oversees administrative functions. Counties typically serve unincorporated areas and fill service gaps in smaller towns or rural municipalities, coordinating closely with state and federal authorities for funding and service standards.
Atlanta, Georgia‘s capital and largest city, exemplifies a mayor-council system with a strong-mayor structure, in which the mayor holds significant executive powers. This setup includes oversight of departments such as law enforcement, city planning, and public works. Atlanta’s city council, representing various districts and at-large seats, functions as the legislative branch, passing ordinances, budgets, and policies. Other cities, like Savannah and Augusta, employ similar models, but Augusta operates as a consolidated city-county government, blending city and county responsibilities under a unified administration.
Georgia also has a few cities that employ council-manager systems, in which an elected city council appoints a professional city manager to handle day-to-day operations. For instance, the city of Macon-Bibb County, a consolidated government, delegates administrative tasks to a manager while the elected officials focus on policy direction. This system is common in medium-sized cities that seek to balance professional management with elected representation.
Counties in Georgia, particularly in rural areas, manage vast unincorporated regions, handling most municipal functions such as law enforcement, road maintenance, and zoning. Gwinnett County, for example, includes several suburban areas and Census-Designated Places (CDPs) like Peachtree Corners that are not incorporated but rely on the county for local governance. These CDPs can mirror urban developments in population and infrastructure, though without their own municipal governments.
Local governance in Georgia also intersects with regional planning agencies, which work with counties and cities on long-term issues like land use, transportation, and economic development. These agencies provide technical expertise and facilitate cooperation between municipal and county governments, ensuring that local planning aligns with regional goals and state mandates.

**Fulton County** is in the north-central portion of the U.S. state of Georgia. As of the 2020 United States census, the population was 1,066,710,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-1) making it the state's most populous county.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-QG2-2) Its county seat and most populous city is Atlanta,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-GR62-3) the state capital. About 90% of the city of Atlanta is within Fulton County; the remaining portion is in DeKalb County. Fulton County is the principal county of the Atlanta–Sandy Springs–Roswell metropolitan statistical area.
Midtown Atlanta and the Downtown Connector
Fulton County was created in 1853 from the western half of DeKalb County. It was named in honor of Robert Fulton, the man who created the first commercially successful steamboat in 1807.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-4)
After the American Civil War, there was considerable violence against freedmen in the county. During the post-Reconstruction period, violence and the number of lynchings of blacks increased in the late 19th century, as whites exercised terrorism to re-establish and maintain white supremacy. Whites lynched 35 African Americans here from 1877 to 1950; according to the Georgia Lynching Project, 24 were killed in 1906. This was the highest total in the state.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-5) With a total of 589, Georgia was second to Mississippi in its total number of lynchings in this period.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-eji-6)

In addition to individual lynchings, during the 1906 Atlanta race massacre, whites killed at least 25 African Americans; the number may have been considerably higher. Two white persons died during the riot; one a woman who died of a heart attack. The violence affected black residential and business development in the city afterward. The Georgia legislature effectively completed disenfranchisement of African Americans in 1908, with constitutional amendments that raised barriers to voter registration and voting, excluding them from the political system_[citation needed_].
At the beginning of 1932, as an austerity measure to save money during the Great Depression, Fulton County annexed Milton County to the north and Campbell County to the southwest, to centralize administration. That resulted in the current long shape of the county along 80 miles (130 km) of the Chattahoochee River. On May 9 of that year, neighboring Cobb Countyceded the city of Roswell and lands lying east of Willeo Creek to Fulton County so that it would be more contiguous with the lands ceded from Milton County.
In the second half of the 20th century, Atlanta and Fulton County became the location of numerous national and international headquarters for leading companies, attracting highly skilled employees from around the country. This led to the city and county becoming more cosmopolitan and diverse.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-8)
In 1992, Fulton County elected the first African-American woman, Jacquelyn Harrison Barrett, to the position of Sheriff in the history of the United States.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-9)

In 2023, rapper Playboi Carti was arrested in Fulton County.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-10) That same year, Donald Trump and 18 co-defendants were indicted by Fulton County district attorney Fani Willis.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-11)As of 2025, the prosecution is being continued by Pete Skandalakis.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-:22-12) Fulton County was a centerpoint in Donald Trump's attempts to overturn the 2020 United States presidential election in Georgia; in January 2026, the FBI conducted a raid on the county's election office.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-13)
Garrett Lake, Mountain Park
According to the U.S. Census Bureau, the county has a total area of 534 square miles (1,380 km 2), of which 527 square miles (1,360 km 2) is land and 7.7 square miles (20 km 2) (1.4%) is water.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-GR1-14) The county is located in the Piedmont region of the state in the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains to the north. The shape of the county resembles a sword with its handle at the northeastern part, and the tip at the southwestern portion.

## About Georgia
In Georgia, counties are governed by elected boards of commissioners or sole commissioners, responsible for countywide issues such as public health, emergency services, infrastructure, and county law enforcement. For example, Fulton County, encompassing Atlanta, is managed by a board of commissioners with a county manager who oversees administrative functions. Counties typically serve unincorporated areas and fill service gaps in smaller towns or rural municipalities, coordinating closely with state and federal authorities for funding and service standards.
Atlanta, Georgia‘s capital and largest city, exemplifies a mayor-council system with a strong-mayor structure, in which the mayor holds significant executive powers. This setup includes oversight of departments such as law enforcement, city planning, and public works. Atlanta’s city council, representing various districts and at-large seats, functions as the legislative branch, passing ordinances, budgets, and policies. Other cities, like Savannah and Augusta, employ similar models, but Augusta operates as a consolidated city-county government, blending city and county responsibilities under a unified administration.
Georgia also has a few cities that employ council-manager systems, in which an elected city council appoints a professional city manager to handle day-to-day operations. For instance, the city of Macon-Bibb County, a consolidated government, delegates administrative tasks to a manager while the elected officials focus on policy direction. This system is common in medium-sized cities that seek to balance professional management with elected representation.
Counties in Georgia, particularly in rural areas, manage vast unincorporated regions, handling most municipal functions such as law enforcement, road maintenance, and zoning. Gwinnett County, for example, includes several suburban areas and Census-Designated Places (CDPs) like Peachtree Corners that are not incorporated but rely on the county for local governance. These CDPs can mirror urban developments in population and infrastructure, though without their own municipal governments.
Local governance in Georgia also intersects with regional planning agencies, which work with counties and cities on long-term issues like land use, transportation, and economic development. These agencies provide technical expertise and facilitate cooperation between municipal and county governments, ensuring that local planning aligns with regional goals and state mandates.

**Fulton County** is in the north-central portion of the U.S. state of Georgia. As of the 2020 United States census, the population was 1,066,710,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-1) making it the state's most populous county.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-QG2-2) Its county seat and most populous city is Atlanta,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-GR62-3) the state capital. About 90% of the city of Atlanta is within Fulton County; the remaining portion is in DeKalb County. Fulton County is the principal county of the Atlanta–Sandy Springs–Roswell metropolitan statistical area.
Midtown Atlanta and the Downtown Connector
Fulton County was created in 1853 from the western half of DeKalb County. It was named in honor of Robert Fulton, the man who created the first commercially successful steamboat in 1807.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-4)
After the American Civil War, there was considerable violence against freedmen in the county. During the post-Reconstruction period, violence and the number of lynchings of blacks increased in the late 19th century, as whites exercised terrorism to re-establish and maintain white supremacy. Whites lynched 35 African Americans here from 1877 to 1950; according to the Georgia Lynching Project, 24 were killed in 1906. This was the highest total in the state.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-5) With a total of 589, Georgia was second to Mississippi in its total number of lynchings in this period.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-eji-6)

In addition to individual lynchings, during the 1906 Atlanta race massacre, whites killed at least 25 African Americans; the number may have been considerably higher. Two white persons died during the riot; one a woman who died of a heart attack. The violence affected black residential and business development in the city afterward. The Georgia legislature effectively completed disenfranchisement of African Americans in 1908, with constitutional amendments that raised barriers to voter registration and voting, excluding them from the political system_[citation needed_].
At the beginning of 1932, as an austerity measure to save money during the Great Depression, Fulton County annexed Milton County to the north and Campbell County to the southwest, to centralize administration. That resulted in the current long shape of the county along 80 miles (130 km) of the Chattahoochee River. On May 9 of that year, neighboring Cobb Countyceded the city of Roswell and lands lying east of Willeo Creek to Fulton County so that it would be more contiguous with the lands ceded from Milton County.
In the second half of the 20th century, Atlanta and Fulton County became the location of numerous national and international headquarters for leading companies, attracting highly skilled employees from around the country. This led to the city and county becoming more cosmopolitan and diverse.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-8)
In 1992, Fulton County elected the first African-American woman, Jacquelyn Harrison Barrett, to the position of Sheriff in the history of the United States.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-9)

In 2023, rapper Playboi Carti was arrested in Fulton County.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-10) That same year, Donald Trump and 18 co-defendants were indicted by Fulton County district attorney Fani Willis.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-11)As of 2025, the prosecution is being continued by Pete Skandalakis.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-:22-12) Fulton County was a centerpoint in Donald Trump's attempts to overturn the 2020 United States presidential election in Georgia; in January 2026, the FBI conducted a raid on the county's election office.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-13)
Garrett Lake, Mountain Park
According to the U.S. Census Bureau, the county has a total area of 534 square miles (1,380 km 2), of which 527 square miles (1,360 km 2) is land and 7.7 square miles (20 km 2) (1.4%) is water.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-GR1-14) The county is located in the Piedmont region of the state in the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains to the north. The shape of the county resembles a sword with its handle at the northeastern part, and the tip at the southwestern portion.

## About Georgia
In Georgia, counties are governed by elected boards of commissioners or sole commissioners, responsible for countywide issues such as public health, emergency services, infrastructure, and county law enforcement. For example, Fulton County, encompassing Atlanta, is managed by a board of commissioners with a county manager who oversees administrative functions. Counties typically serve unincorporated areas and fill service gaps in smaller towns or rural municipalities, coordinating closely with state and federal authorities for funding and service standards.
Atlanta, Georgia‘s capital and largest city, exemplifies a mayor-council system with a strong-mayor structure, in which the mayor holds significant executive powers. This setup includes oversight of departments such as law enforcement, city planning, and public works. Atlanta’s city council, representing various districts and at-large seats, functions as the legislative branch, passing ordinances, budgets, and policies. Other cities, like Savannah and Augusta, employ similar models, but Augusta operates as a consolidated city-county government, blending city and county responsibilities under a unified administration.
Georgia also has a few cities that employ council-manager systems, in which an elected city council appoints a professional city manager to handle day-to-day operations. For instance, the city of Macon-Bibb County, a consolidated government, delegates administrative tasks to a manager while the elected officials focus on policy direction. This system is common in medium-sized cities that seek to balance professional management with elected representation.
Counties in Georgia, particularly in rural areas, manage vast unincorporated regions, handling most municipal functions such as law enforcement, road maintenance, and zoning. Gwinnett County, for example, includes several suburban areas and Census-Designated Places (CDPs) like Peachtree Corners that are not incorporated but rely on the county for local governance. These CDPs can mirror urban developments in population and infrastructure, though without their own municipal governments.
Local governance in Georgia also intersects with regional planning agencies, which work with counties and cities on long-term issues like land use, transportation, and economic development. These agencies provide technical expertise and facilitate cooperation between municipal and county governments, ensuring that local planning aligns with regional goals and state mandates.

In 2023, rapper Playboi Carti was arrested in Fulton County.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-10) That same year, Donald Trump and 18 co-defendants were indicted by Fulton County district attorney Fani Willis.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-11)As of 2025, the prosecution is being continued by Pete Skandalakis.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-:22-12) Fulton County was a centerpoint in Donald Trump's attempts to overturn the 2020 United States presidential election in Georgia; in January 2026, the FBI conducted a raid on the county's election office.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-13)
Garrett Lake, Mountain Park
According to the U.S. Census Bureau, the county has a total area of 534 square miles (1,380 km 2), of which 527 square miles (1,360 km 2) is land and 7.7 square miles (20 km 2) (1.4%) is water.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-GR1-14) The county is located in the Piedmont region of the state in the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains to the north. The shape of the county resembles a sword with its handle at the northeastern part, and the tip at the southwestern portion.

Going from north to south, the northernmost portion of Fulton County, encompassing Milton and northern Alpharetta, is located in the Etowah River sub-basin of the ACT River Basin (Alabama-Coosa-Tallapoosa River Basin). The rest of north and central Fulton, to downtown Atlanta, is located in the Upper Chattahoochee River sub-basin of the ACF River Basin (Apalachicola-Chattahoochee-Flint River Basin). The bulk of south Fulton County, from Atlanta to Palmetto, is located in the Middle Chattahoochee River-Lake Harding sub-basin of the larger ACF River Basin, with just the eastern edges of south Fulton, from Palmetto northeast through Union Hill to Hapeville, in the Upper Flint River sub-basin of the same larger ACF River Basin.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Georgia#cite_note-15)

Fulton County is a no-brainer for anyone looking to experience the heart of Georgia. It’s home to most of Atlanta, the state’s capital and largest city. From the bustling streets of Midtown to the quiet suburbs of Alpharetta, Fulton has diverse living options.
The county boasts world-class attractions like the Georgia Aquarium and the High Museum of Art. Atlanta’s pro sports teams, including the Braves and Falcons, call Fulton home. The county’s economy is a powerhouse, with major corporations headquartered here.
Despite its urban core, Fulton has plenty of green spaces, including the popular Atlanta BeltLine. The county’s history is rich, from Civil War sites to Civil Rights landmarks. Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, the world’s busiest, sits partly in Fulton. Fulton County showcases the many faces of modern Georgia with its southern tip and its northern suburbs.
